I am 57 years old, and I have been farming our land in Quzhou County for more than thirty years. My husband and I have about 7 mu, and we have always done the wheat-maize rotation, just like most families in our village. The wheat went into the ground last October, so now that it is greening up I need to think about the topdressing and irrigation, and also plan for the maize that will go in right after harvest. I am not one to chase the highest yields in the village—my neighbor spent a fortune on extra fertilizer last year and only got a little more grain. I prefer to stay steady. For the winter wheat, I will use the improved variety I have been planting for several years now; the seed shop always has it, and I know how it behaves. I did rotary tillage before planting last autumn, which is what we always do to break up the stubble and level the field. For fertilizer, I will put down compound fertilizer at the base and then topdress with urea when the wheat is at jointing stage. The extension agent told us 18 kg of nitrogen per mu, but I have learned from my own fields that 15 kg per mu is enough on my soil, and fertilizer is expensive. I will irrigate three times—once in early spring, once at jointing, and once during grain filling—because the tube-well water costs more every year but the wheat will not fill properly without that third watering. For the summer maize, I will plant hybrid seed immediately after wheat harvest in early June. The window is terribly tight, sometimes only five or six days, so there is no time to plough. Everyone in the village uses no-tillage for maize now; you just plant straight into the wheat stubble. I will put down fertilizer at planting, about 12 kg of nitrogen per mu, plus some phosphorus and potassium to help the roots. I will irrigate twice if the summer turns dry, which it usually does in July. For pesticides, I spray herbicide once for each crop, and then insecticide only if I see aphids on the wheat or corn borer on the maize. That works out to about two applications per crop. My son in the city tells me not to use too much chemical, but if you skip it the weeds will take over and you will lose everything. I expect about 420 kg per mu for the wheat and 460 kg per mu for the maize. It is not the highest yield in the village, but it is safe, and at my age I cannot afford a bad year.
